# Code Review Report — PR #155 (feat/issue-154-scene-level-expansion)

**Reviewer:** Claude Sonnet 4.6 (raw)
**Date:** 2026-04-23
**Branch:** `feat/issue-154-scene-level-expansion`
**Against:** `development`

---

## Review Summary

PR #155 adds an `expand-to-scenes` operation to `outline-generator` that decomposes a chapter synopsis into a validated JSON array of scene objects during Phase 7a, supported by configurable scene-count bounds and a retry-on-validation-failure loop. The Python implementation, TypeScript wrapper, test coverage, and prompt template are well-constructed. One critical contract gap exists: the three new generation config values required by `chapter-outline-expander` are never passed at dispatch time, leaving the subagent without a source for `scene_expansion_enabled`, `scenes_per_chapter_min`, or `scenes_per_chapter_max`. Additionally, five agent files contain context-hygiene changes from issue #152 that were swept in unintentionally and introduce a stale row in the Per-Chapter Required Sequence table. All 33 new and existing targeted tests pass cleanly.

## Findings

[FINDING-001] New config values not passed to chapter-outline-expander at dispatch
Category: Correctness
Severity: Critical
File: .opencode/agents/story-orchestrator.md
Lines: 163–175 (Phase 7a dispatch block)
Description: `chapter-outline-expander` step g accesses `generation.scenes_per_chapter_min`, `generation.scenes_per_chapter_max`, and checks `scene_expansion_enabled`, but the orchestrator's Phase 7a dispatch block passes only `story_name`, `wanted_chapters`, `expand_outline`, and `model`. The three new config values are also absent from the "Config values to extract and track" list in Phase 1 (lines 51–71). The subagent has no source for these values at runtime and will either fail to evaluate the conditional or use zero/default values that are inconsistent with `config.yml`. This is a broken contract: the feature cannot function correctly as written.
Suggestion: Add all three values to the Phase 1 "Config values to extract and track" list and to the Phase 7a dispatch block:

```markdown
Dispatch `chapter-outline-expander` with:
- `story_name`: story name
- `wanted_chapters`: total chapter count
- `expand_outline`: the `expand_outline` config value
- `scene_expansion_enabled`: the `scene_expansion_enabled` config value
- `scenes_per_chapter_min`: the `scenes_per_chapter_min` config value (default 8)
- `scenes_per_chapter_max`: the `scenes_per_chapter_max` config value (default 16)
- `model`: model config if set
```

Also add the three values to `chapter-outline-expander.md`'s Input table so the agent's contract is explicit.

[FINDING-002] Per-Chapter Required Sequence table contradicts Phase 7e body
Category: Correctness
Severity: Warning
File: .opencode/agents/story-orchestrator.md
Lines: 186 (table row 4), 226 (Phase 7e body)
Description: The summary table at line 186 still says "Write `stories/{name}/chapters/chapter_{N}.md`, then dispatch `consistency-checker`" for Phase 7e. The Phase 7e body (updated in this PR as part of the swept-in #152 context-hygiene changes) explicitly says "Do not write a copy to `stories/{name}/chapters/chapter_{N}.md`". An LLM orchestrator that reads the summary table before the detail section will execute the explicitly-forbidden write step. The two instructions in the same file are directly contradictory.
Suggestion: Update the Phase 7e row in the Required Sequence table to remove the file-write instruction:

```markdown
| 4 | 7e | Dispatch `consistency-checker` with `chapter_file_path: stories/{name}/savepoints/chapter_{N}/chapter_content.md` |
```

[FINDING-003] story-pipeline/SKILL.md Phase 7a row and Config Settings table not updated
Category: Documentation
Severity: Warning
File: .opencode/skills/story-pipeline/SKILL.md
Lines: general (not in changed files)
Description: The Phase 7 sub-phase table in `story-pipeline/SKILL.md` describes Phase 7a as "Delegate full chapter-outline expansion loop and continuitySummary threading" with no mention of the new scene decomposition step. The Config Settings Reference table (near line 305) lists `expand_outline` and `scene_generation_pipeline` but is missing `scene_expansion_enabled`, `scenes_per_chapter_min`, and `scenes_per_chapter_max`. This SKILL.md is the authoritative runtime reference consulted by planning and debugging agents; a stale Phase 7a description leaves them unaware that `chapter_{N}/scene_definitions` may pre-exist before Phase 7b runs, and missing config entries means agents cannot advise the correct default values.
Suggestion: Update the Phase 7a sub-phase row:

```markdown
| **7a** Expand outline | Expand each chapter synopsis and, when `scene_expansion_enabled` is true, decompose into scene objects via `expand-to-scenes` | `chapter-outline-expander` subagent |
```

Add three rows to the Config Settings Reference table:

```markdown
| `scene_expansion_enabled` | bool | true | Whether Phase 7a decomposes each synopsis into scene objects |
| `scenes_per_chapter_min` | int | 8 | Minimum scene count per chapter (expand-to-scenes) |
| `scenes_per_chapter_max` | int | 16 | Maximum scene count per chapter (expand-to-scenes) |
```

[FINDING-004] Step g in chapter-outline-expander.md carries a spurious "3h." label
Category: Style
Severity: Warning
File: .opencode/agents/chapter-outline-expander.md
Lines: 77
Description: The new step is lettered `g.` in the list but its bold heading reads "**3h. (When `scene_expansion_enabled` is true)**". The sub-step list uses single letters (a–i); "3h." implies a different numbering scheme and is inconsistent with the surrounding structure. An LLM agent reading this step will see a mismatch between the outer sequence letter (`g`) and the inner label (`3h`), which can produce ambiguous "next step" reasoning — especially since the step is conditional and may be skipped.
Suggestion: Remove the "3h." prefix from the bold heading. The step should read:

```markdown
   g. **(When `scene_expansion_enabled` is true) Expand synopsis to scenes:** Call `outline-generator` with:
```

[FINDING-005] chapterSynopsis not validated for non-empty in the Python tool
Category: Correctness
Severity: Warning
File: src/tools/outline_generator.py
Lines: 740–754 (argparse definition), 835–849 (dispatch)
Description: `--chapter-synopsis` defaults to `""` (empty string) in argparse. No validation checks that it is non-empty when `operation == "expand-to-scenes"`. The Zod wrapper also marks `chapterSynopsis` as `.optional()` with no minimum length. An accidental omission silently passes an empty synopsis to the prompt, producing meaningless scene output without any error. The analogous required parameter `--chapter-num` does raise an explicit error on omission; `--chapter-synopsis` should do the same.
Suggestion: Add a guard in the `expand-to-scenes` dispatch block (alongside the existing `--chapter-num` check):

```python
if not args.chapter_synopsis:
    print(
        "Error: --chapter-synopsis required for expand-to-scenes",
        file=sys.stderr,
    )
    sys.exit(2)
```

---

[FINDING-006] test_scenes_per_chapter_max_too_high asserts wrong error message fragment
Category: Testing
Severity: Suggestion
File: tests/unit/test_generation_settings.py
Lines: 27–30
Description: The test verifies "Scene maximum above 30 is rejected" but asserts `match="must be >= 1"` — the substring from the minimum-bound clause of the combined error message. The assertion passes because the error string contains both clauses, but it does not actually verify that the maximum bound was violated. A future refactor that separates the validation messages could make the max-violation case silently emit any message containing "must be >= 1" (e.g. an unrelated min violation) and the test would still pass. The intent is to assert on the max bound.
Suggestion: Change the assertion to match the max-bound clause:

```python
with pytest.raises(ValidationError, match="must be <= 30"):
    GenerationSettings(scenes_per_chapter_max=31)
```

## Scope Creep Note

The following five files contain context-hygiene changes from issue #152 that were unintentionally swept into this feature commit:

- `.opencode/agents/chapter-writer.md` — removed `includeContent: true` from `assemble-chapter`; updated Step 8 return contract to compact reference
- `.opencode/agents/consistency-checker.md` — replaced inline `chapter_text` input with `chapter_file_path`; added Step 2 file-load sub-step and renumbered Step 2 sub-steps 1–5
- `.opencode/agents/quality-reviewer.md` — replaced inline `chapter_text` input with `chapter_file_path`; added savepoint overwrite in Step 3; changed return JSON from `accepted_chapter_text` to `accepted_chapter_ref`
- `.opencode/agents/story-orchestrator.md` — multiple Phase 7b/7e/7f/7g context-hygiene sections
- `.opencode/agents/wiki-maintainer.md` — hardened savepoint path in Mode 1 `chapterTextPath`

These changes are correct in isolation but should have been in their own PR. The stale Per-Chapter Required Sequence table row (FINDING-002) is a direct consequence of this sweep: the detail sections were updated but the summary table was not. No other correctness issues were found in the swept-in changes; the consistency-checker and quality-reviewer contract updates are internally consistent with the corresponding orchestrator changes.

## Merge Recommendation

**Do not merge as-is.** FINDING-001 (critical) must be fixed before the feature can work: the subagent dispatching `expand-to-scenes` has no access to the three config values it requires. FINDING-002 and FINDING-003 are required to keep agent runtime references accurate and internally consistent.
